questions.explanation: Enrichment showing a 92 abuse score, a Tor exit node, and a same-day last-seen date corroborates malicious infrastructure and supports automated escalation and blocking. The over-a-month-old option misreads the artifact; the last_seen value (2026-06-25) is current, so the staleness rationale is false.

questions.stem: While correlating an intrusion across three servers, an analyst finds their timestamps differ by up to 14 minutes because Network Time Protocol (NTP) is not configured. Which of the following is the GREATEST impact of this artifact on the investigation?
choices: It prevents accurate event sequencing across hosts
It increases disk consumption on the SIEM
It disables DKIM verification for inbound email
It causes false positives in the vulnerability scanner
questions.explanation: Without synchronized clocks, events cannot be reliably ordered across systems, undermining timeline reconstruction during incident analysis; time synchronization is foundational to log correlation. Disk consumption and DKIM verification are unrelated to clock skew, so those options do not describe the investigative impact.

questions.stem: A finding carries the vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H. Which of the following metrics contributes MOST to its critical (9.8) base score?
choices: The network attack vector combined with no privileges and no user interaction required
questions.explanation: AV:N, AC:L, PR:N, and UI:N together maximize exploitability: anyone on the network can exploit it with low complexity, no credentials, and no victim action. The local-attack-vector and user-interaction options are factually contradicted by the vector, which shows AV:N and UI:N.

questions.stem: Two vulnerabilities have identical impact metrics but differ here: Finding A ends ...S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H and Finding B ends ...S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H. Which of the following is true about Finding B?
choices: It has a lower base score than Finding A
It requires physical access to exploit
Its scope is changed, meaning the exploit can affect resources beyond the vulnerable component's security authority
It cannot be exploited over the network
questions.explanation: S:C (scope changed) means a successful exploit impacts components outside the vulnerable one's security authority, such as a hypervisor escape affecting guest VMs, which raises severity. The lower-base-score option is backwards: a changed scope increases the score relative to the otherwise identical S:U finding.

questions.stem: Scan rows: Host A is an external web server with CVE-2026-1001 at CVSS 7.5, listed in the CISA KEV catalog with active exploitation; Host B is an internal file server with CVE-2026-2002 at CVSS 9.1 and no known exploit. Which of the following should be remediated FIRST?
choices: Host B, because it has the higher CVSS base score
Neither, until the next maintenance window opens
Host A, because it is externally exposed and actively exploited per KEV
questions.explanation: An internet-facing host with a vulnerability in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog represents real, present risk that outweighs a higher raw CVSS on an internal asset with no known exploit. Choosing Host B treats the base score as the sole driver, ignoring the exploitability and exposure context that should lead prioritization.

questions.stem: An unauthenticated scan reports "Apache 2.4.49 Path Traversal (CVE-2021-41773)" on a host, but the server team insists the package was patched to 2.4.58. Which of the following is the BEST way to validate the finding?
choices: Accept the scan result and open a critical ticket
Run a credentialed scan to read the installed package version directly
Delete the scanner plugin causing the alert
Reboot the server and rescan from the outside
questions.explanation: A non-credentialed scan infers versions from banners and can produce false positives; an authenticated (credentialed) scan reads the actual installed package version, definitively confirming or refuting the finding. Accepting the result outright skips validation and risks acting on a false positive, which the version discrepancy specifically calls into question.

questions.stem: Two equally exposed findings: CVE-2026-3100 at CVSS 8.1 with EPSS 0.02 (2nd percentile) and CVE-2026-3200 at CVSS 6.5 with EPSS 0.86 (97th percentile). Which of the following should the analyst prioritize and why?
choices: CVE-2026-3100, because its CVSS base score is higher
CVE-2026-3200, because its high EPSS predicts a far greater likelihood of exploitation
Both are equal because EPSS is irrelevant to prioritization
questions.explanation: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) estimates near-term exploitation probability; an 0.86 EPSS signals the lower-CVSS finding is much more likely to be attacked and should go first. Choosing by CVSS alone ignores real-world exploitability, the exact trap EPSS is designed to correct.

questions.stem: A Nessus row reads: Plugin 12345 | "SMBv1 Enabled" | Severity: High | CVSS 7.5 | Output: server permits SMBv1 negotiation. Which of the following controls BEST remediates this finding?
choices: Disable the SMBv1 protocol on the host
Add a firewall rule allowing port 445 inbound
Install a self-signed certificate on the share
Enable verbose logging on the file share
questions.explanation: SMBv1 is a deprecated, exploitable protocol (the EternalBlue family targets it); disabling it directly removes the vulnerable component, the cleanest remediation. Opening port 445 inbound would expand exposure rather than remediate, and logging does not eliminate the underlying protocol weakness.

questions.stem: A scan of an OT/ICS subnet of programmable logic controllers (PLCs) reports numerous "service crashed/no response" results, and one PLC halted during the scan window. Which of the following scanning concepts was likely violated?
choices: Active scanning of fragile operational technology that should use passive methods
External scanning of a DMZ host
Static analysis of application source code
questions.explanation: Active probing can disrupt delicate OT/ICS devices, as the halted PLC shows; passive or agentless approaches are preferred for critical infrastructure to avoid service interruption. The other options describe unrelated scan types that would not cause a PLC to crash, so they do not explain the outage.

questions.stem: A finding shows CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N. Which of the following statements about exploitation is correct?
choices: It requires no authentication and no user action
It results in a full integrity and availability loss
It is exploitable only with physical access to the host
It requires some privileges and victim user interaction, and only confidentiality is impacted
questions.explanation: PR:L means low privileges are needed, UI:R means a user must take an action, and C:H/I:N/A:N means only confidentiality is impacted; the vector decodes directly to those facts. The full integrity and availability loss option contradicts I:N/A:N, and physical access contradicts AV:N.

questions.stem: The identical CVE-2026-4400 (CVSS 8.8) appears on a public marketing kiosk and on the primary domain controller, both unpatched. Which of the following BEST determines remediation order?
choices: They are equal because the CVSS base score is identical
The domain controller first, because its asset value and blast radius are far higher
The kiosk first, because kiosks reboot frequently
Neither until the next quarterly remediation cycle
questions.explanation: When CVSS is equal, asset value and potential blast radius break the tie; a domain controller compromise can cascade across the entire identity infrastructure, so it outranks a standalone kiosk. Treating them as equal ignores context awareness (asset criticality), a core prioritization input beyond the base score.

questions.stem: An IDS flags exploitation of a flaw in a third-party library for which the vendor has no patch and no CVE has yet been assigned. Which of the following BEST classifies this situation?
choices: A false positive, since no CVE exists
An end-of-life component reaching its support cutoff
A zero-day vulnerability being actively exploited
questions.explanation: An actively exploited flaw with no vendor patch and no assigned CVE is the definition of a zero-day; the absence of a CVE reflects newness, not safety. Labeling it a false positive misreads missing-CVE status as proof of no vulnerability, which the active exploitation contradicts.

questions.stem: An analyst must test a customer-facing web application for SQL injection and cross-site scripting by intercepting and manipulating HTTP requests. Which of the following tools is BEST suited?
questions.explanation: Burp Suite is an intercepting web proxy and scanner built to manipulate HTTP(S) requests and test for web-layer flaws such as SQLi and XSS. Nessus is a host vulnerability scanner, not an interactive web-app testing proxy, so it is the wrong tool for request manipulation; Volatility (memory) and Wireshark (packets) are further out of lane.

questions.stem: A security engineer needs to audit an AWS account for misconfigured S3 buckets, overly permissive IAM policies, and CIS benchmark deviations. Which of the following tools is the BEST fit?
questions.explanation: Prowler performs AWS security best-practice and CIS benchmark assessments, exactly matching cloud posture auditing. Nikto scans web servers, GDB debugs native binaries, and Angry IP Scanner sweeps IP ranges, so none assess cloud IAM or S3 configurations.

questions.stem: A team wants to find input-handling crashes in a compiled C binary by feeding it large volumes of malformed input automatically. Which of the following techniques is being described?
questions.explanation: Fuzzing supplies malformed or random inputs at scale to trigger crashes that reveal memory-safety and input-validation bugs, a dynamic analysis technique. Credentialed scanning checks known vulnerabilities via authentication and does not generate malformed inputs to provoke crashes.

questions.stem: A scan report shows: "22/tcp open ssh OpenSSH 7.4", "80/tcp open http", "443/tcp open https" with no severity ratings or CVE references. Which of the following tools MOST likely produced this output?
questions.explanation: Port, service, and version listings without severities or CVEs are characteristic Nmap output (host discovery and service/version detection); Nmap maps the attack surface but does not itself rate vulnerabilities. Nessus output would include plugin IDs, CVSS scores, and CVE references, which are absent here.

questions.stem: A legacy application requires TLS 1.0, which a scan flags as a cryptographic weakness, but the vendor cannot patch it for six months. Which of the following is the BEST interim measure?
choices: Accept the risk and take no action
Place the application behind a reverse proxy that enforces modern TLS, a compensating control
Remove the application from production immediately
Reclassify the finding as a false positive
questions.explanation: When a direct fix is not yet possible, a compensating control (here a TLS-terminating reverse proxy) reduces the risk while preserving the business function. Simply accepting the risk leaves the weakness fully exposed, and the scan correctly identified a real flaw, so reclassifying it as a false positive is inaccurate.

questions.stem: A critical patch deployed last night broke an order-entry service, and the change ticket lists no validation step. Which of the following parts of the patch process was MOST clearly skipped?
choices: Testing in a staging environment before production rollout
questions.explanation: Deploying straight to production and breaking a service indicates the change bypassed staging and testing, the step that catches compatibility regressions before they reach users. Asset discovery and CVE enumeration occur earlier and would not have prevented a functional regression from an untested patch.

questions.stem: After analysis, leadership decides a residual cyber risk on a niche legacy system will be covered by purchasing a cyber-insurance policy rather than by further remediation. Which of the following risk responses is this?
questions.explanation: Shifting the financial consequence of a risk to a third party (the insurer) is risk transfer. Mitigate would reduce the likelihood or impact directly, and accept would retain the risk with no offsetting mechanism, so neither matches buying insurance.

questions.stem: A web app log shows a server-side request triggered by user input: GET /fetch?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/. Which of the following vulnerabilities is being exploited?
choices: Server-side request forgery (SSRF) targeting cloud metadata
questions.explanation: Coercing the server to fetch the 169.254.169.254 link-local cloud metadata endpoint via a user-supplied URL is server-side request forgery, often used to steal instance credentials. XSS executes in the victim's browser, not on the server fetching internal URLs, so it does not describe this server-initiated request.

questions.stem: A web application firewall (WAF) blocks this request: GET /download?file=../../../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1. Which of the following attack types and remediations is correct?
choices: Directory traversal; validate and canonicalize file-path input
Cross-site request forgery; add anti-CSRF tokens
questions.explanation: The ../ sequences walking up to /etc/passwd are path or directory traversal; the fix is strict input validation and path canonicalization to block traversal characters. Parameterized queries address SQL injection, a different flaw class, so that remediation does not apply to file-path manipulation.

questions.stem: A debugger shows a function using strcpy() copying 300 bytes of attacker input into a 64-byte stack buffer, overwriting the saved return address. Which of the following BEST mitigates this class of flaw?
choices: Bounds checking with safe functions plus stack canaries
Adding a CAPTCHA to the form
questions.explanation: An unbounded copy overflowing a fixed stack buffer is a classic stack buffer overflow; bounds-checked functions plus stack canaries (and ASLR/DEP) directly address it. Output encoding mitigates injection and XSS, not memory corruption, so it does not fix the overflow.

questions.stem: Two scans of the same host: Scan 1 (no credentials) reports 40 findings, many marked "potential/unconfirmed"; Scan 2 (with credentials) reports 27 findings, all version-confirmed. Which of the following BEST explains the difference?
choices: Scan 2 missed vulnerabilities because credentials hide findings
Scan 2 is inherently less accurate than Scan 1
Scan 1 produced more false positives because it could not confirm versions
The host configuration changed between the two scans
questions.explanation: Non-credentialed scans infer from external responses and tend to over-report unconfirmed issues (false positives), while credentialed scans read actual installed versions, yielding fewer, higher-confidence findings. The claim that credentials hide vulnerabilities is backwards; authentication generally improves accuracy and reduces false positives.

questions.stem: An organization that stores cardholder data must demonstrate quarterly external vulnerability scans performed by an approved vendor. Which of the following frameworks imposes this requirement?
questions.explanation: PCI DSS mandates quarterly external scans by an Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV) for entities handling cardholder data. ISO 27001 is a general management-system standard without that specific quarterly ASV scan mandate, so it does not impose this particular requirement.

questions.stem: A vulnerability report shows CVE-2026-5050 was marked "remediated" in April but reappears on the same 12 hosts in May and June. Which of the following does this trend MOST indicate?
choices: A false negative produced by the scanner
Recurrence indicating the fix is not persisting, for example reverted by re-imaging
A brand-new zero-day on those hosts
questions.explanation: A closed finding that returns on the same hosts is recurrence, signaling the remediation is not sticking (often re-introduced by golden images, configuration drift, or rollback). It is not a false negative; the scanner is correctly detecting the vulnerability each cycle, which is precisely how the recurrence is visible.

questions.stem: A full active scan launched at 10:00 on a Monday saturated the network and slowed a customer-facing application during peak hours. Which of the following scan considerations was MOST clearly mismanaged?
choices: Scheduling the scan outside peak operational windows
Plugin selection for the scan policy
questions.explanation: Running a heavy active scan during peak business hours ignored scheduling and operations considerations meant to avoid performance impact; scans should target maintenance windows. Credentialing affects accuracy, not the timing that caused the peak-hour slowdown, so it is not the mismanaged factor here.

questions.stem: EDR shows host 10.5.1.20 maintaining an active reverse shell to an external IP and beginning to enumerate domain administrators. Which of the following should the incident responder do FIRST?
choices: Isolate the host from the network to cut the active C2 channel
questions.explanation: With an active C2 session and lateral-movement reconnaissance underway, containment (network isolation) comes first to stop attacker activity and limit spread, ahead of eradication or recovery. Re-imaging is an eradication step and is premature before the scope of compromise is understood and the channel is cut.

questions.stem: Responders must collect evidence from a live, compromised Linux server before shutdown: (1) the disk image, (2) the RAM contents, and (3) archived logs on a NAS. Which of the following should be collected FIRST per the order of volatility?
choices: The archived logs on the NAS
None until the server is powered off
questions.explanation: The order of volatility dictates capturing the most ephemeral data first; volatile memory (RAM) is lost on shutdown, so it precedes the disk image and the far more stable archived logs. Powering off first would destroy the volatile evidence the investigation needs, so waiting is the worst option.

questions.stem: A seized laptop's evidence form lists who collected it, timestamps, computed hash values, and every person who handled it with dates. Which of the following does this documentation establish?
choices: Chain of custody for the evidence
questions.explanation: A continuous record of custody, handling, timestamps, and integrity hashes is the chain of custody, which preserves admissibility by proving the evidence was not altered. A business continuity plan addresses operational resilience, not evidence handling, so it does not describe this form.

questions.stem: Logs show an attacker sent a spear-phishing email with a weaponized document that, when opened, installed a backdoor that then connected outbound to a controller. The backdoor's outbound connection to its controller maps to which of the following Cyber Kill Chain stages?
questions.explanation: Establishing the channel through which the adversary remotely controls the implant is the command and control (C2) stage of the Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain. Delivery refers to transmitting the weaponized document (the phishing email), which is an earlier, distinct stage.

questions.stem: An analyst observes lsass.exe being read by a non-system process that then writes a file later found to contain credential material. Which of the following MITRE ATT&CK tactics does this BEST map to?
questions.explanation: Reading LSASS memory to harvest credentials is OS credential dumping, which falls under the Credential Access tactic in MITRE ATT&CK. Exfiltration covers moving data out of the environment, a later objective that this in-host credential theft does not yet represent.

questions.stem: Threat intel attributes an intrusion to a specific nation-state group (the adversary) that used a custom RAT (the capability) hosted on leased servers to target an energy firm (the victim). The leased servers correspond to which of the following Diamond Model features?
questions.explanation: In the Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis, the physical or logical resources an adversary uses to deliver capabilities (here the leased servers) are the Infrastructure vertex. Capability refers to the tooling or malware (the custom RAT), which is a separate feature of the diamond.

questions.stem: A ransomware infection is contained on three isolated hosts, but the malware binary and its persistence registry keys remain on those hosts. Which of the following is the appropriate NEXT phase?
choices: Recovery by restoring data from backups
Detection by tuning SIEM correlation rules
Eradication by removing the malware and persistence artifacts
questions.explanation: After containment, the next IR phase is eradication: removing the malware, persistence keys, and other artifacts before systems are restored. Recovery (restoring from backups) must wait until eradication is complete, or the restored systems risk re-infection from leftover artifacts.

questions.stem: Eradication is complete on a workstation that held an attacker foothold. Which of the following BEST returns it to trusted production use?
choices: Re-image from a known-good baseline and restore validated data
Reconnect it unchanged to monitor the attacker
Submit its file hashes to VirusTotal
questions.explanation: Recovery returns systems to operation from a trusted state; re-imaging from a known-good baseline plus restoring validated data ensures no residual compromise. Reconnecting an unremediated host to observe the attacker abandons containment and risks renewed compromise, so it is not a safe recovery step.

questions.stem: During an incident likely headed to litigation, counsel instructs the team to suspend the 30-day automatic log-deletion job for all affected systems. Which of the following BEST describes this directive?
choices: A legal hold preserving potentially relevant evidence
questions.explanation: Suspending routine deletion to preserve data that may be relevant to litigation is a legal hold, ensuring evidence is not destroyed by normal retention processes. A maintenance window is a scheduled change period, unrelated to preserving evidence for legal proceedings.

questions.stem: Before and after copying a disk image to analysis media, the responder computes SHA-256 hashes and confirms they match. Which of the following does this step accomplish?
choices: It encrypts the evidence at rest
It detonates the malware to observe behavior
It validates the integrity of the acquired image
questions.explanation: Matching pre- and post-copy hashes proves the image was not altered during acquisition, validating data integrity, a cornerstone of forensically sound evidence handling. Hashing does not encrypt data; it produces a one-way fingerprint, so the encryption claim mischaracterizes the step.

questions.stem: An analyst confirms one compromised host but must learn how many other systems the same stolen credentials or malware touched. Which of the following IR activities is the analyst performing?
choices: Determining the scope of the incident
questions.explanation: Identifying how far an intrusion has spread (which accounts, hosts, and data are affected) is scoping within detection and analysis, and it shapes containment and eradication. Eradication is the later removal of artifacts and cannot be executed properly until scope is understood.

questions.stem: Before any incident, a team runs a discussion-based walkthrough of a simulated ransomware scenario to test roles and decision-making without touching production. Which of the following preparation activities is this?
questions.explanation: A discussion-based, scenario-driven walkthrough that exercises roles and decisions without affecting live systems is a tabletop exercise, part of IR preparation. A penetration test actively probes systems for weaknesses and is not a discussion-only rehearsal, so it does not fit the description.

questions.stem: After recovery, the team determines the breach began with an unpatched VPN appliance exploited via a known CVE, and documents this as the underlying cause. Which of the following post-incident activities is this?
questions.explanation: Identifying the underlying reason an incident occurred (here the unpatched, exploitable VPN appliance) so it can be prevented in the future is root cause analysis, a post-incident activity. Incident declaration happens at the start to formally recognize an incident, not during post-incident review of causes.

questions.stem: A server is actively exfiltrating data and cannot be powered off because volatile evidence must be preserved, yet the exfiltration must stop now. Which of the following containment actions BEST balances both needs?
choices: Run a full antivirus scan and wait for results
Delete the suspicious files in place
Move the host to an isolated VLAN or apply host-based network isolation while keeping it running
questions.explanation: Network-level isolation (an isolated VLAN or EDR host isolation) halts exfiltration while keeping the system powered, preserving volatile memory for later acquisition. Pulling power stops exfiltration but destroys volatile evidence, failing the requirement to preserve it.

questions.stem: A SOC analyst confirms a malware alert is a true positive affecting a single non-critical test VM with no network connectivity. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate response per a tiered IR plan?
choices: Immediately declare a major incident and notify executives
Shut down the entire data center
Handle it as a low-severity event per the playbook without major-incident escalation
Contact law enforcement and the media
questions.explanation: A contained, non-critical, isolated test VM does not meet major-incident criteria; the proportionate response follows the low-severity playbook path rather than over-escalating. Declaring a major incident and alerting executives over a single isolated test system is a disproportionate over-reaction not justified by the impact.

questions.stem: Responders captured a RAM image from a host suspected of fileless malware and need to list running processes, network connections, and injected code from that image. Which of the following tools is the BEST choice?
questions.explanation: Volatility is the memory-forensics framework purpose-built to enumerate processes, connections, and injected code from a RAM image, ideal for fileless malware analysis. FTK Imager acquires disk and memory images but is not the analysis engine for parsing memory artifacts, so it is the wrong stage of the workflow.

questions.stem: An analyst is writing the executive summary of a breach report for the board of directors. Which of the following is MOST appropriate to include in that section?
choices: Raw packet captures and full registry hive dumps
A concise business-impact overview, scope, and high-level recommendations
The Sigma rules used for detection
questions.explanation: An executive summary is for leadership and should convey business impact, scope, and key recommendations in non-technical language. Raw packet captures and registry dumps belong in the technical or forensic appendix, not the executive summary aimed at decision-makers.

questions.stem: A report shows the gap between an intrusion's start (02:00) and the SOC's first alert acknowledgment (06:30). Which of the following metrics does this 4.5-hour interval represent?
questions.explanation: The elapsed time from compromise to detection is the mean time to detect (MTTD); shrinking it is a core SOC goal. Mean time to respond measures the interval from detection to a response action, a different and later segment of the timeline.

questions.stem: An incident confirms exposure of EU residents' personal data. Which of the following communications is MOST time-sensitive given regulatory obligations?
choices: A press release to national media
A lessons-learned email to the SOC
A post on the company's social media accounts
Regulatory notification within the mandated breach-reporting deadline
questions.explanation: Exposure of EU residents' personal data triggers GDPR breach-notification duties with a strict 72-hour regulatory deadline, making regulator notification the most time-sensitive channel. A press release may follow but is not the legally mandated, deadline-bound obligation that drives urgency here.

questions.stem: A critical patch is ready, but a contract guarantees a vendor-managed system will not be modified without the vendor's sign-off, delaying deployment. Which of the following inhibitors to remediation does this represent?
choices: A memorandum of understanding (MOU) or service-level agreement (SLA) constraint
questions.explanation: A contractual obligation requiring vendor approval before changes is an MOU or SLA inhibitor to remediation, constraining when and how the fix can be applied. Degrading functionality refers to a fix that harms operations, not a contractual approval gate, so it does not describe this delay.

questions.stem: A monthly vulnerability report includes a chart of the ten most frequently recurring critical findings across the fleet over six months. Which of the following reporting elements is this?
choices: A trend and top 10 key performance indicator (KPI)
questions.explanation: Tracking the most common recurring critical findings over time is a trends and top-10 KPI, used to communicate program effectiveness and focus remediation. A chain-of-custody log documents evidence handling in incident response, unrelated to recurring-vulnerability trend reporting.

questions.stem: A vulnerability affecting the payment-processing application must be communicated. Which of the following stakeholders is MOST appropriate to receive the technical remediation details and own the fix?
choices: The application's development and operations team
questions.explanation: The team that builds and operates the affected payment application is the right stakeholder to receive technical remediation detail and own the fix. The media and general public are not appropriate recipients of technical remediation tasking and would raise unnecessary disclosure risk.

questions.stem: An incident report section lists, in order with timestamps: initial phishing email received, malicious link clicked, beacon established, data staged, containment executed. Which of the following report elements is this?
questions.explanation: A chronological, timestamped sequence of events from initial access to containment is the incident timeline, which supports analysis and reporting. An executive summary is a high-level, non-chronological overview, so this ordered event list is a distinct element.

questions.stem: Leadership asks how long, on average, from when a critical vulnerability is identified to when it is fully patched across all hosts. Which of the following metrics answers this question?
questions.explanation: The average interval from identifying a vulnerability to completing its patch across hosts is mean time to remediate. Mean time to detect measures finding the issue, not fixing it, so it does not answer a question about patch completion time.

questions.stem: Mid-incident, a manager wants to call a local news outlet and the police immediately. Which of the following should the team consult FIRST before any external disclosure?
choices: The public relations team to draft the customer notice
Legal counsel to guide external communications and obligations
questions.explanation: Legal counsel must guide external disclosures to manage liability, privilege, and regulatory or law-enforcement obligations before any message leaves the organization. Engaging public relations or contacting the media before that legal review risks compromising the investigation and violating disclosure requirements, the classic wrong-channel trap.

questions.stem: A vulnerability report ranks findings by a composite value combining CVSS, asset criticality, and exploit availability rather than CVSS alone. Which of the following BEST describes this value?
choices: A contextual risk score for prioritization
questions.explanation: Blending CVSS with asset value and exploitability into one prioritization figure is a contextual risk score, more decision-useful than raw CVSS for communicating priority. Alert volume counts alerts handled and has nothing to do with ranking individual vulnerabilities by risk.

questions.stem: After a breach traced to absent multifactor authentication, the report proposes enforcing MFA, segmenting the VPN, and adding logging. In which of the following report sections do these items BEST belong?
questions.explanation: Forward-looking corrective actions to prevent recurrence belong in the recommendations section of the incident report. The evidence section documents the artifacts proving what happened, not proposed future controls, so the suggested fixes do not belong there.

questions.stem: A SOC manager reports that daily alerts rose from 4,000 to 11,000 after a new sensor deployment, straining analysts. Which of the following metrics is being communicated?
questions.explanation: The count of alerts generated over a period is the alert-volume metric, useful for capacity planning and tuning to reduce analyst fatigue. MTTD measures detection speed, not the quantity of alerts, so it does not capture the workload increase described.

questions.stem: An auditor requests evidence that all in-scope cardholder-data systems were scanned and remediated to satisfy a card-brand mandate. Which of the following report types BEST fulfills this request?
questions.explanation: Demonstrating that cardholder-data systems were scanned and remediated to meet the card-brand mandate is the purpose of a PCI DSS compliance report. A lessons-learned memo captures IR improvements and does not provide the formal scan and remediation attestation an auditor requires.

questions.stem: Following a confirmed breach of customer accounts, the company must inform affected customers clearly and consistently while protecting its reputation. Which of the following functions BEST leads this external messaging?
questions.explanation: Crafting clear, consistent customer-facing messaging while managing reputation is the public relations function's role in incident communications. The vulnerability scanning team handles technical detection, not external customer communication, so it is not suited to lead public messaging.
